LUMEN TERMINOLOGY GUIDE V1.1

This version supersedes guide 1.0. It retains the identifiers but revises definitions and examples following the Regional Archive workshop and person evaluation. The earlier version remains archived.

Creator is reserved for organic creation of a fonds. Author identifies intellectual responsibility for content. Producer identifies physical or digital production. In photography, a studio may be creator of the fonds, the photographer author of the image, and a supplier producer of the copy. A role applying to the copy is not inherited by the original.

Agent is the general class; Person and Organization are subtypes. A studio, family, association, company, or administrative unit is not classified as a person because of the form of its name.

Padrón de habitantes uses municipal register of residents. Libro de actas is rendered as minute book. Expediente is normally rendered as case file. Diligencia uses official certification note or procedural record according to context. Oficio de remisión uses forwarding memorandum. Bando uses public notice.

Exact date, approximate date, date range, year-level date, and seasonal expression form the temporal vocabulary. Unknown indicates absence in the source; not applicable means that the field does not correspond to the object.

Preferred place name is the selected name for a period. Historical variant identifies an earlier name. Namesake place is another place sharing the name. A spelling change does not create an entity.

Unlinked mention is a mention without sufficient evidence. Provisional person is an entity awaiting confirmation. Verified link requires contextual evidence in addition to the name. Rejected candidate retains a discarded alternative.

Open metadata does not imply an open digital object. Thumbnail permitted limits authorization to a thumbnail. Metadata only requires the file and thumbnail to remain hidden. Conditions of use is displayed where it limits download or publication.

Rule 1

Preferred labels use the singular and avoid abbreviations except for institutional forms. Definitions explain boundaries and do not turn contingent examples into rules. Official names are retained. Access translations of titles are marked and do not replace the source title.

Rule 2

Every entry has an identifier, ES label, EN label, definition, example, provenance, and status. Labels do not mix languages in one literal. A semantic change is reviewed in both languages. Pending terms do not reach the public package.

Rule 3

The distinctions among creator, author, and producer are closed, as are the translations of padrón de habitantes, libro de actas, oficio de remisión, and bando, and the separation between unlinked mention and provisional person. Diligencia remains context dependent.

Rule 4

The specialist translation of expediente de información pública remains pending, along with English names for some cartographic units and treatment of honorifics. They will be reviewed when more examples exist.

Rule 5

The guide applies to the model, ingestion, demonstrator, and publication. Interfaces may abbreviate labels but retain the identifier and provide access to the definition. Search uses preferred labels, alternatives, and source terms without generating duplicates.

Rule 6

Every modification states its reason, examples, decision, and affected artifacts. The previous_version and next_version relations must be reciprocal. An incompatible redefinition requires a new version and documented migration.
